liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (4 reviews): Well played with a nice jam; good enough to be included on the So Many Roads box set; Jam after the verses is led by Brent's jangly piano, which is relatively rare; drummers speed up at the end [12][13][19][23]
- **Eyes Of The World** (4 reviews): Reviewer calls it out of this world, with deep space jamming ranking among favorite jams of the year; Nineteen-minute version after a smooth transition, fast-paced; by the second break Garcia struggles to keep up with Weir and Brent [12][13][19][23]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): Reviewer says it sounds like a cover band performed it [16]
- **Althea** (1 review): Jerry spaces words oddly and Bobby is off too, per the reviewer [16]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Lightning was visible out over the plains to the east during this song [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-08-12.fob.nak700.menke.motb-0137.107166.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1979-08-12.145471.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1979-08-12.164360.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 181 min [3]. Said about its sound: Wind noise throughout, most noticeable during Peggy-O [3]
- **gd1979-08-12.157083.aud.hicks-fong.flac1644**: audience recording; 24 songs; 172 min [7]. Said about its sound: Wind causes crackly noises and tape artifacts; small gaps are patched with lo-fi tape; rough, of historical interest [7]
- **gd79-08-12.sbd.clugston.9288.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 163 min; rated 3.87/5 by 23 [9]. Said about its sound: Described as a nice recording; Sound is crispy but Phil is not coming through much, and it is not in stereo [19][22]

## Around the show

- Attendee says someone falling from the rocks was the highlight; claims no rain fell that night, only the next day [17]
- Rain the following day led to the move to McNichols arena in Denver; this was the series' first night [17]
- Attendee recalls lightning over the eastern plains during Rider and a breeze rising around the Colorado rain line [18]
- After the show, people cleared the parking lot and park; attendee hitched a ride to McNichols the next morning [18]
- Reviewer worked as a roofer in Fort Collins in summer 1979 and heard the show announced on the radio [21]
- Reviewer's only Red Rocks visit, on the way to California; found the scene overwhelming [23]
- Space jamming in Eyes is likened to the Playin' from 11-6-79; 1979 shows are generally loved [12]
- First set is wobbly, but the band improves and plays strongly in the second set; Estimated>Eyes is classic [16]
- Reviewer ranks it as the most explosive Dead show of their life, apart from Radio City on Oct 29, 1980 [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-08-12.fob.nak700.menke.motb-0137.107166.flac16**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: Nak CM 700s => Sony TC-D5 >> MAC. Aud Master Cassettes (MAC) Medium Stock Brands: MAC = 3 x Maxell UDXLII 90 Analog [1]. Also: Source is a Nakamichi 700 recording, with Bob Menke credited in the filename [1]
- **gd1979-08-12.145471.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-270 mics (row 13, seats 68 & 69 - 1st set held head high, 2nd set mounted on pole)> Sony TC-158SD (Maxell… [2]. Also: A six-second patch in Drums comes from the Nakamichi 700 source, shnid 107166 [2]
- **gd1979-08-12.164360.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell XLII-C90) [3]
- **gd1979-08-12.157083.aud.hicks-fong.flac1644**: taped by John Hicks & Dennis Fong; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 06/2022; source: Handheld deck (mono) > MAC > 1st-Gen back-up tapes [7]. Also: Audience recording possibly made on a Panasonic portable held up at head level [7]
- **gd79-08-12.sbd.clugston.9288.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard [9]
